Group Risk Management Policy

GRP-POL-001|Version6.0|Internal

## 9.Group risk taxonomy

A single taxonomy is applied Group-wide so that risks can be identified consistently, aggregated meaningfully and compared between divisions and legal entities. Every risk in the Group Risk Register, every incident, every issue and every loss event must be classified to a Level 2 category at minimum.

Group Risk Taxonomy —Level 1 and Level 2 Categories 
Credit Market Liquidity &Operational Compliance &Strategic &

Risk Risk Funding Risk Conduct Reputational 
Wholesale credit Trading book Funding concentraton Process & execution Regulatory compliance Business model 
Retail credit Interest rate (RRBB)Intraday liquidity ·Technology & cyber Financial crime & AML Mergers & acquisitions 
Counterparty credit Foreign exchange Asset encumbrance Third-party & outsourcing Sanctions Climate & environmental 
Concentration  Equity & commodity Contingent liquidity Fraud (intemal/extemal)•Market conduct Reputation 
Country/sovereign •Credit spread collateral People & workplace Customer outcomes Model risk 
Data &records Data privacy 
Taxonomymaintained by Tobias Lindqvist,Analyst-Privacy Engineering (t.lindgvist@cadencefg.com,+44 2o 7555 0171).

Figure 5 — Group Risk Taxonomy, Levels 1 and 2.

## 9.1 Taxonomy governance

* Owned by the Group CRO and maintained by Tobias Lindqvist, Head of Enterprise Risk Framework (t.lindqvist@cadencefg.com).

* Changes at Level 1 require Board Risk Committee approval; Level 2 changes require Group Executive Risk Committee approval.

* Reviewed annually and following any material change to the business model or regulatory environment.

•Divisions may not create local categories; where none fits,a change request is raisedto theGroupRisk function.

•Historical classifications are restatedwhen the taxonomy changes,so trendreporting remains comparable.

## 9.2 Classification rules

Where etm event could fall into more than one category it is classified by root cause, not by the form of the consequence. A customer refund arising from a system defect is operational risk (technology), not conduct risk, although the conduct consequence is recorded alongside it. Where a single event has consequences in several categories, the primary classification is used for aggregation and secondary tags are applied for analysis.

## 10. The risk management process

TheGroupapplies a single,continuous process to everyrisk category. Thedepthofapplication is proportionate to materiality,butno step may be omitted.
